main_text.l: ex differente materiâ. Contrà enim est hy-
pothesis Apostoli: quia ex eâdem prot-
sus massâ facit figulus vasa, pro ar-
bitrio suo & potestate. Neque enim de-
bet massæ differentiam istam. Quare
injuriam illi nō faceret; si tantùm vasa
dedecoris, facere, aut honoris. Ita De-
us justitiam non violat, quomodocun-
que agat: omnium miserendo; aut o-
mnes indurando; aut denique aliquo-
rum miserendo, aliquos indurando; &
eos quidem, quos vult. Neque enim ul-
li quicquam debet: non majori; non
minori. Proinde, de debito & justitiâ,
aliena hîc est consideratio.
Quartus locus fit ille periculose ςρεˆ μεν δ a quibusdam: Κενὴν
ὀργὴς κατηρτισμένα εἰς ἀπώλειαν. v. 22. credo, ob explicatio-
nes Pelagianas, humanęq; rationis, re-
cedentes nõ solùm à literâ; sed etiam
à mente contextus. A quo enim vasa sunt
præparata; nisi à figulo, Deo? Cur vasa
iræ; nisi ad interitū? quemadmodum
misericordiæ, in gloriam. v.23. pro po-
testate, quam habet figulus, in eandem
massam.

page.notes: Marginal label "4. De Vasis ad interitum paratis. ibid. v.22." on the left, partly illegible at its edges. Greek phrases in the text are printed in Greek; the Greek in the paragraph (the first line after "quibusdam:" and the reference "εἰς ἀπώλειαν") is copied as closely as the scan allows, and the opening Greek word "ςρεˆ" and "μεν" are doubtful. The word "ςρεˆ" is a faint, damaged Greek word and may be misread. Several words in the body are slightly blurred but read with reasonable confidence. The right margin strip shows fragments of letters from the facing page and is not transcribed.
